original_context: Graph theory: neighborhood N_G(v)={u∈V:{u,v}∈E} in a simple undirected graph G=(V,E).
definition: For a simple loopless undirected graph G=(V,E) and a vertex v∈V, the open neighborhood N_G(v) is the set {u∈V:{u,v}∈E} of all vertices adjacent to v. It excludes v itself.
reasoning: Existing screened definitions give vertex degree through the cardinality of the neighbor set, but do not separately define the underlying set-valued graph-neighborhood construction. The definition must use the open-neighborhood convention; the closed neighborhood N_G[v]=N_G(v)∪{v} is a different operation. Avoid confusion with topological neighborhoods and directed-graph in/out neighbors.

sources.relevance: Directly verified the set of adjacent vertices excluding the base vertex and the distinction from the closed neighborhood.

related_screened_meanings.relation: Vertex degree counts the members of this set, but is a cardinal rather than the neighbor set

mathematical_assumptions: G is a simple undirected loopless graph.
v belongs to the vertex set, including isolated vertices whose neighborhood is empty.
The set excludes v; closed neighborhood differs and directed-graph variants are not implicitly included.
